stem: A breeder compares selections from two rooms but does not record which environment each plant experienced. What important interpretation problem does this create?
choices: Environmental effects can be confused with inherited differences
The plants can still be compared, but the missing room records mainly reduce confidence in estimating how strongly each genotype responds to management
Parentage information becomes less useful because environmental records are needed before inherited relationships can be interpreted at all
Recorded phenotypes remain valid for selection because repeated visual similarity is usually enough to separate genetic effects from environmental effects
rationale: Without environmental context, observed phenotypic differences may be incorrectly attributed to genetics when growing conditions contributed to the outcome.
